question: What is the main reason we use injection safety supplies in the hospital?

options.A: To make hospital storage rooms look neat and organized
options.B: To protect patients and nurses from blood-borne infections
options.C: To reduce the cost of buying drugs
options.D: To speed up intravenous fluid administration

explanation: You got this! Injection safety items like proper syringes and safety boxes are specifically designed to stop infections like HIV and hepatitis from spreading during procedures.

question: Why does running out of basic injection gear cause dangerous situations on the ward?

options.A: Hospital management will automatically close down the clinic
options.B: Staff might feel tempted to reuse single-use syringes out of desperation
options.C: Nurses will completely stop writing patient notes
options.D: Patients will refuse to take any medications

explanation: Spot on! When supplies run dry, desperate situations can lead to unsafe shortcuts like reusing disposable syringes, which puts everyone at risk.

question: What makes an auto-disable syringe different from a regular disposable syringe?

options.A: It locks automatically after one use to prevent reuse
options.B: It doesn't need a needle to deliver medication
options.C: It can be easily washed and sterilized for another patient
options.D: It is made entirely of recycled plastic

explanation: Exactly right! Auto-disable syringes have a clever built-in stop that keeps the plunger from pulling back a second time, keeping everyone safe.

question: Where should you drop a used needle immediately after giving an injection?

options.B: Back inside its original plastic wrapper
options.C: In the general office waste basket
options.D: On top of the treatment trolley tray

explanation: Well done! Always drop used sharps straight into a safety box to prevent accidental needle pricks on the ward.

question: In ward inventory, what does hitting your 'minimum stock level' tell you?

options.A: It is the exact number of items used in a single day
options.B: It is the warning sign that tells you to place a new order
options.C: It is the maximum amount the store can hold
options.D: It shows the total financial budget for the clinic

explanation: That's correct! Think of minimum stock as your alarm bell—when supplies drop to this point, it's time to reorder so you don't run out.

question: How should a nurse manager figure out how many safety boxes to order for next month?

options.A: By doubling the number of expired items thrown away last year
options.B: By matching the exact number of doctors on duty
options.C: Based on past patient use and expected service volume
options.D: By guessing a random number that fits on the form

explanation: Spot on! Smart ordering looks at past consumption trends and expected patient numbers so you don't overstock or run short.

question: What is the very first thing you must do before filling out a supply requisition form?

options.A: Travel directly to the central medical warehouse
options.B: Throw all remaining safety boxes in the incinerator
options.C: Write a complaint letter to the hospital director
options.D: Count the physical stock currently on your ward shelves

explanation: You got it! You always need to see what is physically on hand before you can figure out what is missing.

question: Why does a requisition form need a supervisor's review and signature before heading to the store?

options.A: To stop nurses from talking to warehouse workers
options.B: To delay delivery and keep storerooms empty
options.C: To give the medical director extra paperwork to sign
options.D: To confirm that what you asked for matches your actual usage

explanation: Exactly! Authorization checks help catch mistakes, prevent over-ordering, and keep everything transparent.

question: What is the main job of a bin card attached to a storage shelf?

options.A: To give instructions on treating needle stick injuries
options.B: To advertise the brand name of the syringe maker
options.C: To show a running balance of stock movements in real time
options.D: To list phone numbers of delivery drivers

explanation: Well done! A bin card acts as a quick ledger right at the shelf, tracking every item added or taken away.

question: What is a big benefit of using digital inventory systems instead of paper records?

options.A: It ensures clinical injections never cause skin pain
options.B: It completely stops nurses from ever needing to count items
options.C: It lets central managers view stock data across sites quickly
options.D: It stops medical supplies from reaching their expiration date

explanation: Spot on! Digital systems link different clinics together, making it super easy to spot trends and shortages early.

question: In medical storage, what does the FEFO rule stand for?
explanation: You nailed it! FEFO means items closest to their expiry date get used first so nothing goes to waste.

question: Why is it important to keep cardboard safety boxes away from damp floors?

options.A: Moisture helps safety boxes assemble themselves
options.B: Water makes the needles inside sharper and safer
options.C: Wet cardboard attracts helpful insects to the room
options.D: Dampness weakens the cardboard and causes dangerous leaks

explanation: That's right! Water ruins cardboard rigidity, which can lead to nasty punctures or fluid leaks from used sharps.

question: What is the best immediate step for a clinic facing a sudden stockout of syringes?

options.A: Tell nursing staff to wash and reuse standard syringes
options.B: Borrow supplies from a nearby cooperating facility
options.C: Stop providing all injection treatments indefinitely
options.D: Wait patiently for the next quarterly delivery

explanation: Brilliant! Emergency borrowing between friendly neighboring clinics bridges the gap safely without resorting to dangerous reuse.

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to reduce waste in a hospital store?

options.A: Checking inventory expiration dates every month
options.B: Keeping storage rooms dry, clean, and out of direct sunlight
options.D: Ordering huge quantities far beyond what past data suggests

explanation: You got it! Over-ordering leads straight to expired stock and wasted money—definitely a practice to avoid!
